body:
## Purpose

This PR fixes a regression of ClimaCore v1.0.9: on CPUs, `MatrixFields.single_field_solve!` and the solvers that call it allocate on the heap when bounds checking is on, which fails a zero-allocation test of ClimaAtmos (`test/prognostic_equations/correct_implicit_advection_tests.jl`, now run with ClimaCore v1.0.8 since CliMA/ClimaAtmos.jl#5013).

## Disclosure

This PR and its description were generated using Claude.

## Content

- `single_column_solve!` is inlined into the loop over columns, so the factors of a band matrix stay in arrays on the stack of the solving thread when bounds checking is on (as in `Pkg.test`), instead of on the heap.
title: Inline single_column_solve!

body:
## Purpose

This PR adds the `@noconsts` macro, an analogue of `@noinline` that disables constant propagation on a function, and uses this macro in place of `@drop_constprop` and `Base.@constprop :none`. It also disables constant propagation on the functions that only pass their arguments along, which lowers compilation latency and memory usage.

## Disclosure

This PR and its description were mostly generated using Claude.

## Content

- `@noconsts` replaces `Base.@constprop :none` and `@drop_constprop`, with a docstring that explains when to use it
- Constant propagation is disabled on functions that pass their arguments along without computing on constant values, so they are no longer re-inferred for every new constant input:
  - CUDA extension functions that configure, compile, and launch kernels
  - functions that construct, check, reassign, slice, and evaluate broadcasts
  - `copyto!`, `fill!`, and `setindex!` of `Field`s, `FieldVector`s, and data layouts
  - views, `level` slices, and constructors of `Field`s and data layouts
  - `Operators` and `MatrixFields` internals, like geometry helpers and field name lookups
  - the thread pool and point update loop functions
  - the tri-diagonal band solve

## Comparison against main

Each row compares this PR against the `main` branch, in ClimaCore's CI and the downstream builds that it triggers ([8379](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/8379), [822](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/822), [204](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacoupler-downstream/builds/204), and [174](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaland-downstream/builds/174) for the PR; [8375](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-ci/builds/8375), [814](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-downstream/builds/814), [200](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacoupler-downstream/builds/200), and [170](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaland-downstream/builds/170) for `main`), and in the end-to-end performance pipeline ([826](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/826) for the PR; [823](https://buildkite.com/clima/climacore-end-to-end-performance/builds/823) for `main`). Rows over several jobs give the median of the PR values, the median of the `main` values, and the median of the per-job changes (so a change can differ from the ratio of the two medians beside it). Setup memory is the memory allocated while a simulation is set up, most of it by compilation, and it is the same in every build of one commit.
